correctness.rationale: Conditioning on the common Exp(1) variable and taking Laplace transforms gives the stated inclusion–exclusion probability. With z=x², p=(1+q+z)²−4qz and w=p+2λ(1+q+z), the objective is λ²(w+p)/[w(w+λ²)]. Independently differentiating and expanding the quotient verifies H(0)=2(q+1)(λ+q+1)B and H′(0)=−4(q+1)(λ+q+1)C for the numerator normalized as in the proof. Denominators are positive (p is the product of two strictly positive distance factors). For q≤1 the sign is strictly negative; for q>1, B decreases strictly in λ from a positive value to −infinity. The positive quadratic root is the stated λ_c. When B=0 the discriminant of C in λ is 21−54q−11q²<0, so the coefficient of x⁴ is strictly negative and there is still a strict local maximum. Below the boundary, evenness, decay at infinity and strict local inferiority of x=0 give a reflected pair of noncentral global maximizers. No global uniqueness or optimality at or above λ_c is inferred. In the independent case the denominator as a polynomial in z is z²+2(1+λ−q)z+(1+λ+q)², giving the stated comparator including a strict quartic midpoint optimum at equality. Substituting λ=q−1 into B gives −2q(q−1)(3q−1)<0. The bound 0<λ_c<q−1 makes the rescaled roots bounded in both limiting regimes; division of the defining polynomial by q−1 or q³ gives the respective unique nonnegative limiting roots 2/3 and (sqrt(57)−1)/14. Replay: expand H=(w′+p′)w(w+λ²)−(w+p)w′(2w+λ²) and its derivative at z=0 by symbolic polynomials; a separate direct derivative in x under the exponential expectation also gives J″(0)=4λ²B/[(q+1)(λ+q+1)³(2λ+q+1)²]. At q=4 the positive root is approximately 1.590549454, versus 3 independently. The supplied finite diagnostic was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The two environments have exactly the same single-site founding probabilities, yet different midpoint stability. For q>1 and λ between the two thresholds, the shared-weather midpoint is strictly locally optimal while the independent-weather midpoint is unstable. The exact root and quartic classification make a structural contribution for this nonlinear joint objective that neither a covariance sign nor a one-site curve can provide. The result is intentionally a dimensionless one-dimensional benchmark, not field validation or a global placement prescription.
